body_text:
A deductive system is *sound* if every formally provable sentence
is a semantic consequence: $\Gamma \vdash \varphi \implies \Gamma
\models \varphi$. It is *complete* if every semantic consequence
is formally provable: $\Gamma \models \varphi \implies \Gamma
\vdash \varphi$.

Soundness ensures that the formal rules never introduce falsity
from true premises. Completeness, established for first-order
logic by Kurt Gödel in 1929, is one of the crowning intellectual
achievements of modern logic: it guarantees that truth across all
mathematical models can always be captured by finite symbolic
manipulation.
